images.seen: A paved walkway through a stone-walled coastal village at grey dawn, heavy cloud with one weak sun break over a rough sea. Thursday.
lines: The sun is trying its luck at the horizon and the cloud is unmoved.
The sea keeps its winter colour under a sky like this, whatever the calendar says.
A grey start on the coast usually burns off by ten. Usually.

images.seen: A woman in a navy swimsuit on a striped towel on a lawn, sunscreen in hand, squinting up at a dark grey cloud bank with blue sky still visible behind it, plumbago hedge and white gable house. Saturday.
lines: The cloud arrived about four minutes after the towel went down, which is policy.
Sunscreen out, sun gone: the sky has a sense of humour today.
The blue sky is still back there somewhere, but the grey has the floor.

images.seen: An empty school rugby field with white posts under a flat grey sky, dry koppies and a red-brick school building behind. Wednesday.
lines: Flat grey over the rugby field: perfect kicking weather, no wind to blame.
The sky has gone the colour of the staff-room ceiling and settled in.
A perfectly average sky doing perfectly average things.

images.seen: A chameleon halfway along a bare branch, heavy grey cloud filling the sky, garden leaves and a terracotta roof below. Friday.
lines: The one animal that can match the sky's mood is having no trouble today.
Every leaf is holding still; the whole garden is waiting to see what the sky decides.
The clouds are here but they're not doing anything.
